Scripts that exist: dev (vite), build (tsc -b && vite build), lint (oxlint), preview. There is NO test script and NO test dependency (vitest, jsdom, testing-library, msw are absent from package.json and node_modules).

dependencies.runtime: None. The existing React 19 stack is sufficient: useState, useEffect, useRef, useId, native form elements. No router, state library, form library, date library or HTTP library.
dependencies.mock: No MSW. TASK.md accepts "an HTTP client or equivalent replaceable request boundary". The boundary is the SessionsApi interface in types.ts; the mock is one in-memory implementation of it. This avoids a service worker file and a new dependency.

dev-dependencies.note: No test stack exists in the repo, so one is required for the mandatory automated test. Versions are resolved by npm at install time (latest compatible with Vite 8); exact versions are unverified.
dev-dependencies.dependency: Test runner. Reuses the existing Vite config and transform, so no Babel/Jest setup is needed.
DOM environment for rendering React in Vitest.
Render and query by what the trainer sees (roles, labels, text).
Readable DOM assertions (toBeInTheDocument, toBeDisabled) via its vitest entry point.

layers.layer: types.ts, constants.ts, format.ts, validation.ts. Pure, no React, no imports from other layers (validation and format import constants/types only).
mockSessionsApi.ts. Implements SessionsApi from types.ts. Knows nothing about React or UI.
useSessions.ts. Receives a SessionsApi by argument, never imports the mock directly. Owns list data and load status.
SessionsWorkspace (container), SessionFilter, SessionList, CreateSessionForm. Presentational parts receive data and callbacks via props.
App.tsx imports the default mock instance and passes it to SessionsWorkspace as the api prop. This is the only place the mock is chosen. Tests pass a fake api instead.

architecture.dependency-direction: App -> SessionsWorkspace -> (useSessions, SessionFilter, SessionList, CreateSessionForm) useSessions -> types CreateSessionForm -> validation, format, constants, types SessionList -> format, constants, types mockSessionsApi -> types, constants validation, format -> constants, types Rule: arrows never point back up. UI never imports mockSessionsApi (only App does). mockSessionsApi never imports React.
architecture.communication: Workspace calls useSessions(api) and receives { status, sessions, reload, createSession }. Workspace passes the filtered list to SessionList and createSession plus onCreated/onCancel to CreateSessionForm. The form calls createSession(input), awaits it, and on success calls onCreated; the workspace then closes (unmounts) the form.
architecture.conventions: Use import type for types (verbatimModuleSyntax). Use string-literal unions with an as const array, not enums (erasableSyntaxOnly). Relative imports, .tsx/.ts extensions for local files to match main.tsx. Component files export only components (oxlint only-export-components); constants live in constants.ts. No TypeScript strict migration.

state.name: sessions list
state.why: Server-like data; shared by list and create. Updated only by successful load and successful create (new session prepended with a functional update).

state.name: load status
state.why: Drives loading, error and success views. 'Empty' is not stored: it is derived as success with zero visible sessions.

state.name: reload trigger
state.why: Retry sets status to loading and increments the counter; the load effect depends on [api, attempt]. The effect uses a cancelled flag in cleanup so StrictMode's double effect run and stale responses are ignored.

state.name: active status filter
state.why: UI-only choice, used only by the container to derive the list.

state.name: form open
state.why: Container shows or hides the form. Unmounting the form on close/success resets its local state automatically.

state.name: form values
state.why: Local to the form; startsAt holds the datetime-local string. Kept on create failure because the form stays mounted.

state.name: form errors
state.why: Computed on submit by validateSessionForm; a field's error is cleared when that field is edited.

state.name: submit error
state.why: Create-failure message; cleared on the next submit attempt.

state.name: pending-create flag
state.location: CreateSessionForm (useState boolean for rendering + useRef boolean as synchronous guard)
state.why: State updates are async, so two submit events in the same tick could both pass a state check. The ref is checked and set synchronously at the top of the submit handler; the state disables the submit and cancel buttons and changes the label to 'Creating...'. The ref is reset in finally.

state-management.derived: const visible = filter === 'all' ? sessions : sessions.filter(s => s.status === filter), computed in SessionsWorkspace during render. No effect, no extra state, no useMemo (small list). Because it derives from the full list, a new session appears under an active filter only if its status matches, and always under All.
state-management.blocking-repeated-submit: handleSubmit: if (submittingRef.current) return; validate; if errors, show them and return; submittingRef.current = true; setPending(true); try { await createSession(...); onCreated() } catch { setSubmitError(msg) } finally { submittingRef.current = false; if still mounted setPending(false) }. After success the form is unmounted, so setPending must be guarded (use a mounted ref or skip the reset on success path). Exactly one api.createSession call per valid submission.
state-management.toolbar-visibility: Filter and the New session button are rendered only when load status is success (including the empty case). This prevents creating during loading, which would be overwritten by the load result, and creating while the list is in error.

data-contracts.statuses: SESSION_STATUSES = ['scheduled', 'completed', 'cancelled'] with labels Scheduled, Completed, Cancelled. Filter options: All, Scheduled, Completed, Cancelled. DEFAULT_STATUS = 'scheduled' (a newly created future session is naturally scheduled).
data-contracts.mock-behavior: createMockSessionsApi(options: { latencyMs?: number; seed?: Session[]; failFirstList?: boolean; failFirstCreate?: boolean }). In-memory array store, closure state, no globals. listSessions resolves a copy of the store after latency (default 600 ms). createSession resolves after latency (default 800 ms): assigns id (counter, e.g. session-6), status DEFAULT_STATUS, prepends to the store, returns the new Session. Failure: when failFirstList is true the first listSessions call rejects with Error('Failed to load sessions'), later calls succeed (so Retry demonstrably recovers). failFirstCreate behaves the same for the first createSession call, which does not modify the store. Seed: 5 sessions covering all three statuses, with startsAt computed relative to module load time (completed in the past, scheduled in the future); titles are plausible training topics. Default instance: mockSessionsApi = createMockSessionsApi(optionsFromUrl()). optionsFromUrl reads window.location.search once (guarded by typeof window) param mock: 'list-error' -> failFirstList, 'create-error' -> failFirstCreate, 'empty' -> seed []. These params exist only to let the manual browser check reach the error and empty states; they are not part of the product UI.
data-contracts.date-time-decision: The form uses a native input type="datetime-local" (value format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm, no timezone). The value is interpreted in the browser's local timezone: new Date(value). Stored and exchanged as ISO UTC via toISOString(). "Future" means new Date(value).getTime() strictly greater than Date.now() at submit time (injected as now in validation for testability). Display uses Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { dateStyle: 'medium', timeStyle: 'short' }) in the browser's local timezone and locale; the <time> element carries dateTime={startsAt}. A value that does not parse (empty string) counts as missing.

ui-ux-decisions.layout: One centered column (max-width about 720px, 16px+ padding). Hierarchy: main > h1 "Training sessions" > toolbar (SessionFilter + "New session" button) > CreateSessionForm (when open, directly under the toolbar, inline, no modal) > content area (loading | error | SessionList or empty message).

states.state: role="status" text "Loading sessions..." in the content area. Toolbar hidden.
role="alert" block: "Could not load sessions." plus "Check your connection and try again." and a "Try again" button that calls reload. One error state only. Toolbar hidden.
Short text "No sessions to show." in the content area, used both for an empty load and for a filter with no matches. Toolbar stays visible so the trainer can create or change the filter.
ul of li. Each item: title (strong), status label (small text badge with a plain border, no color coding), start date/time in a time element. Order: as returned/prepended; no sorting.

ui-ux-decisions.filter: Native select with a visible label "Status" and options All, Scheduled, Completed, Cancelled; default All. Native control chosen for built-in keyboard and screen-reader support.
ui-ux-decisions.create-form: Entry point: "New session" button in the toolbar; it is disabled/hidden while the form is open. Form heading "New session". Fields: text input labelled "Title" (maxLength not set, so the 80-character rule is reported by validation rather than silently truncated) and datetime-local input labelled "Start date and time". Buttons: "Create session" (submit) and "Cancel". Form has noValidate so only the app's own messages show. Each field's error is rendered in a p directly under the field, linked with aria-describedby and aria-invalid on the input; the first invalid field receives focus after a failed submit. Create-failure message is rendered in a role="alert" paragraph above the buttons. While pending: both buttons disabled, submit label "Creating...". Cancel closes and discards values. Success closes the form and resets it (unmount).
ui-ux-decisions.visual-constraints: No animations or transitions. Neutral palette via CSS custom properties on :root: page background #f6f7f9, surface #ffffff, text #1f2933, muted text #52606d, border #cbd2d9, primary button background #3e4c59 with white text, error text #a61b1b. System font stack, 16px base, line-height 1.5, spacing in multiples of 8px, visible focus outline (do not remove). Plain CSS in src/index.css with simple class names; no CSS framework.
ui-ux-decisions.note: A newly created session hidden by an active non-matching filter is simply not shown (per requirements). No extra notice is added, to avoid scope growth; see risks.

validation-rules.rule: Value is trimmed (String.prototype.trim) before checks. After trim, length 0 -> "Enter a title." Length 1 to 2 -> "Title must be at least 3 characters." Length greater than 80 -> "Title must be at most 80 characters." Lengths 3 and 80 are valid. Surrounding spaces never count. The trimmed value is what is sent to the API. Length is JS string length (UTF-16 units).
Empty or unparseable -> "Choose a start date and time." Parsed time less than or equal to now -> "Start date and time must be in the future." Strictly later than now is valid.
API rejection -> "Could not create the session. Your entries are kept, please try again." Shown in the form; values preserved; submit re-enabled.
"Could not load sessions." with the hint "Check your connection and try again." and button "Try again".
validation-rules.timing: Validation runs on submit; both fields are validated together so both messages can show at once. A field's error is cleared when that field changes. No API call is made when validation fails. All message strings live in constants.ts (single place to reword).
validation-rules.signature: validateSessionForm(values: { title: string; startsAt: string }, now: Date = new Date()): { title?: string; startsAt?: string }. Empty object means valid.

testing-and-verification.tooling: Vitest (jsdom) + @testing-library/react + @testing-library/user-event + @testing-library/jest-dom. Run with npm test (vitest run). Tests live next to the feature in src/features/sessions/. Tests render SessionsWorkspace with a hand-written fake SessionsApi (not the mock with latency), so they need no timers; pending states are controlled with deferred promises. Queries use roles, labels and text only; no snapshots, no assertions on internal state.

tests.test: Fake list returns sessions with all three statuses. Assert loading text first, then titles and status labels visible. Select "Completed" in the "Status" select: only completed titles remain. Select "All": every title is back.

test.name: creates a session and shows it

tests.test: Open "New session", type a valid title (with surrounding spaces) and set a far-future date via fireEvent.change on the datetime-local input (user-event typing into it is unreliable in jsdom). Fake createSession returns a deferred promise. Submit twice (click plus fireEvent.submit on the form in the same tick): assert createSession called once with the trimmed title and an ISO startsAt, and "Creating..." is shown with the button disabled. Resolve: new title appears in the list, the form is gone, reopening the form shows empty fields.
createSession rejects: the failure message is visible, typed title and date are still in the inputs, and a second submit (now resolving) succeeds.
First listSessions rejects: "Could not load sessions." visible; click "Try again": sessions render.

Titles of 3 and 80 chars (also padded with spaces) valid; "", " ", 2 chars, 81 chars invalid with the exact messages; empty, past and equal-to-now date invalid; now plus one minute valid, using an injected now.

testing-and-verification.checks: npm run lint, npm run build, npm test. Results reported verbatim, including failures.

manual-browser-check.procedure: 1. npm run dev; open the URL Vite prints in a real browser. Record URL, browser name and version, date. 2. Load: observe "Loading sessions..." then the list; confirm each row shows title, status, date/time. 3. Filter: pick each status, then All; record which titles were visible each time. 4. Create validation: open New session and submit empty; then title "ab"; then 81 characters; then valid title with no date; then a past date. Record each message and its position. 5. Boundaries: titles of exactly 3 and exactly 80 characters (with surrounding spaces) are accepted. 6. Create success: valid title and future date; double-click Create; record "Creating..." state, that exactly one new row appeared, form closed, and reopening shows an empty form. Repeat with a non-matching filter active and record that the row is hidden until All is chosen. 7. Error and empty states: open /?mock=list-error (error persists on every retry; use /?mock=list-error-once to see Try again recover), /?mock=create-error (first create fails, entered values kept, resubmit succeeds), /?mock=empty ("No sessions to show."). 8. Check the browser console for errors.
manual-browser-check.record: For every step: what was actually seen (quote messages), pass or fail, anything unexpected, console errors. Written to frontend-accelerator-onboarding/workflow-log.md by the developer (not by this plan).

testing-and-verification.reported-as-not-done-or-not-checked: Anything not run is reported as such. Expected by design: no screenshots, no multi-browser or mobile/responsive check, no accessibility audit beyond labels/roles used in tests, no coverage measurement, no real backend or network behavior, no CI or deployment, vitest.config.ts not type-checked by tsc -b, exact installed dependency versions not pinned by this plan. Timezone behavior is checked only in the developer's local timezone.

risks-and-open-questions.item: No existing mock mechanism: assumed an in-memory implementation behind the SessionsApi interface is an acceptable "equivalent replaceable request boundary". Alternative if a true HTTP-level mock is required: MSW (adds a dependency and a service worker file). No requirement is changed either way.

No existing test stack: Vitest + Testing Library added as the smallest fit for Vite. Exact versions and compatibility with Vite 8 and TypeScript 6 are unverified until npm install; if incompatible, the coder reports it rather than switching tools silently.
URL parameters ?mock=... are a manual-verification aid, not a product feature. If undesired, the alternative is temporarily editing mock options during the manual check.
Filter and New session are hidden during loading and error to avoid a create-versus-load race. The requirements do not forbid showing them earlier; assumption chosen for correctness and simplicity.
A created session is prepended to the list; the checklist allows any order. Mock seed dates are relative to page load, so seeded "scheduled" items always look upcoming.
Title length uses JS string length; emoji or other astral characters count as two. Acceptable for a training exercise.
When a status filter is active and the created session does not match, nothing indicates it was created. This follows the requirement literally; a notice would be added scope and is not planned.
vitest.config.ts is outside tsconfig.node.json include, so it is not type-checked by tsc -b. Adding it would modify an existing config, which the constraints discourage; left as is.
The datetime-local control renders differently across browsers; behavior beyond the one manual browser is unchecked.
No blocking questions: no STOP condition was hit.
